issue: Section 5: Leo moved from Ginger Island with Willy's help; the parrot family that raised him stayed on the island. Reply claims 'He did, with his parrot family', relocating the parrots to the valley.
suggested_fix: He did, with Willy's help and mine. The parrots who raised him stayed behind in his warm home across the sea, but I am glad such a place exists, and gladder still that it gave us Leo.

issue: Section 6: he attends festivals, alone, mostly for food and quiet; at the Winter Star he is present but feels unwelcome ('I'd join in... but I don't think I'm welcome'). 'Most years I keep away' reads as skipping the feast entirely.
suggested_fix: Most years I go, but I keep to the edge of it. I would join in, yet I never quite feel welcome among the tables.

issue: Section 4 / weather canon: rain does not occur in winter in the valley (winter weather is snow, wind, or sun), so the 'winter, raining' context is an impossible game state and the reply anchors to 'a cold winter rain'. Re-anchor the context line to snowing.
suggested_fix: A wet, heavy snow is harder than the dry kind, I will grant you. The damp cold finds its way in, so I keep the fire steady and my blanket close.

issue: Section 4 / weather canon: same impossible 'winter, raining' state as linus-state-012; the whole row (context and all three Linus replies) is anchored to a winter rain that cannot occur. Re-anchor context and later replies to snow.
suggested_fix: Not at all, my friend. Come in out of the snow. I have tea on, and a cold night makes it taste all the better.

issue: Section 6 / festival geography: the Festival of Ice is held in Cindersap Forest south of town, not at his mountain lake. 'The whole town comes up to the cold water where I feel most at home' relocates the festival to his own lake.
suggested_fix: A little, enough for a good supper. It is a fine thing to see the whole town out on the ice for a day, living a morning of the winter I know so well.

issue: Bible hard boundary (and section 1): never place his home 'by the water' or 'by the lake'; his tent sits on the cliff above and he climbs down to fish. Reply says 'a fine gift for a man who lives by the water below'.
suggested_fix: I will thank it for its sacrifice, as I always do, and waste not a scrap. A fresh fish is a fine gift for a man who cooks his supper over a campfire.

issue: Section 3: he refuses ONLY the Treasure Chest; every other gift he accepts, even disliked ones (they draw a reaction, not a refusal). Both replies refuse the costly shop item ('no, thank you' and 'Keep it, or give it to someone who will treasure it'); the second reply needs the same acceptance rewrite.
suggested_fix: Er... that is very kind of you. Something so fine and costly sits strangely in a small life like mine, but I will keep it, and treasure the thought behind it most of all.

issue: Section 3: he refuses ONLY the Treasure Chest. Both replies refuse the modern gadget ('Um... no, thank you' and 'Keep it for someone who has a use for it'); the second reply needs the same acceptance rewrite.
suggested_fix: Hm. I am afraid I would not know what to do with such a thing, but you carried it up the hill for me, so I will keep it, and the kindness with it.

issue: Section 9 / bible: never invent lore the canon does not support. 'I climbed to the source once, just to pay my respects to it' invents a past pilgrimage to the glacier source; the glacier-fed water itself is canon, the journey is not.
suggested_fix: All that way. I drink from it each morning and pay my respects to the mountains that send it down.

issue: Section 5/8: the George trash-can event records the raccoon accusation, his embarrassment, and 'if I didn't eat the food, it would go to waste'; canon records no promise to stop. 'I promised him I would not rummage in his can anymore, and I have kept my word' invents a resolution.
suggested_fix: No, he was not. I was sorry to have upset him; I only took what would have gone to waste, and these days I keep clear of his can.

issue: Section 5/8: same invented promise to George as linus-lore-049 ('I gave him my word I would leave his can be, and I keep my promises'); no such promise is canon.
suggested_fix: It settled, in time. I keep clear of his can these days, and I never wished the old man any trouble.

issue: Section 6 / checklist item 8: at festivals he keeps to the edges for food and quiet; the salmonberry jelly line is ordinary spring dialogue, not a festival contribution. Bringing jelly 'for everyone to taste' and calling sharing 'the closest thing I have to a festival tradition' invents festival behavior; the second reply's tradition line should be softened to match.
suggested_fix: Only a taste of spring. The salmonberry harvest was kind to me this year, so I made a sweet and tangy jelly and brought a jar down. Here, try a spoonful before the dancing starts.

issue: Section 6: at the Fair he watches the animals and keeps to a quiet corner; the display tables are the farmers' grange displays. Claiming he contributed 'a few of my best wild mushrooms and forage' invents festival participation.
suggested_fix: Not I. The wild's bounty is its own to give, not mine to show. But it pleases me to see the valley's harvest laid out and admired.

issue: Section 5: the Spirit's Eve line 'Good show, old friend' is addressed to the Wizard, his one old friend; here 'I find it a good show, old friend' redirects the address to a 4-heart player, muddying the relationship anchor.
suggested_fix: A good show, I call it. The Wizard is an old friend of mine, and I suspect his hand in all this strangeness. The town rarely lets itself be this playful.

issue: contains 'once': 'The land has never once sent me to bed hungry'
suggested_fix: Every bite of it. The land has never sent me to bed hungry when I paid it proper attention.

issue: contains 'once': 'I have never once gotten sick'
suggested_fix: Why would it? I only take what looks fresh, and I have never gotten sick from it. It is a shame to let good food rot.

issue: contains 'once': 'I climbed to the source once'
suggested_fix: All that way. I drink from it each morning and pay my respects to the mountains that send it down.

issue: contains 'once': 'the exact shape I was looking for once made my whole week'
suggested_fix: Hard to say. A stick with the exact shape I had been looking for made my whole week.

issue: contains 'once': 'the way I was once'
suggested_fix: He is still a little wary, the way I was in my early days here. But his heart is open to the wild, and that is what matters.

issue: contains 'once': 'It did once, more than I let on'
suggested_fix: It did in the early years, more than I let on. Now I have made my peace with it.

issue: contains 'once': 'More than once, I am sorry to say'
suggested_fix: It has happened a few times, I am sorry to say. Someone threw rocks at it one night, and another time a joker sprayed paint all over it.

issue: contains 'once': 'it grows true once it takes root'
suggested_fix: I thought you might. Warmth grows slowly with me, but it grows true when it takes root.

issue: contains 'once': 'I have never once thought so'
suggested_fix: I have never thought so. And I have made my peace with those who do.

issue: contains 'once': 'It surprised me too, once'
suggested_fix: It surprised me too, in my first years out here. The wild keeps no ledger. It simply provides, and I simply give thanks.

issue: contains 'once': 'I was no different from you once'
suggested_fix: You can learn to survive in the wild. I did, and I was no different from you when I began.

issue: contains 'once': 'never once seems anxious about it'
suggested_fix: They say patience, mostly. They say there is no hurry. A tree takes a hundred years to grow and never seems anxious about it.

issue: contains 'once': 'I lived much as everyone does, once' (the sanctioned backstory phrase; listed only for once density)
suggested_fix: There was a time I lived much as everyone does. But the noise of that life wore me thin, and I left it behind.

issue: contains 'once': 'The cold comes on fast once fall turns'
suggested_fix: I need to start gathering lumber for the winter. The cold comes on fast when fall turns, and a full woodpile is a warm night waiting to happen.

issue: contains 'once': 'Not once you have truly unplugged'
suggested_fix: Not after you have truly unplugged from the busy way of living. Then you start to enjoy the simple things: the sun on the snow, a ripe stored fruit, a stick shaped just so.

issue: contains 'once': 'The whole valley seems to exhale at once'
suggested_fix: You feel it too, then. The first warm morning after a long winter lifts something in the chest. The whole valley seems to exhale together.

issue: contains 'once': 'It is nice, once a year, to see the town come out'
suggested_fix: I am. The night is an old companion of mine. It is nice, one night a year, to see the town come out and greet it too.

issue: contains 'once': 'moved by a warm gathering once a year'
suggested_fix: Even I. A man can love his solitude and still be moved by a warm gathering each winter. The Winter Star has a way of reaching everyone, if they let it.

issue: contains 'once' twice: 'Once I lived much as everyone does' and 'I have never once regretted it'
suggested_fix: For you, I do not mind telling. There was a time I lived much as everyone does, but the noise of that life wore me thin, so I made the leap into the quiet. I have never regretted it.

issue: contains 'once' twice: 'It stung once' and 'You never once used it to wound me'
suggested_fix: Let them. It stung in the early years, but from where I stand now, with a friend like you beside me, the old name has lost all its bite. You never used it to wound me.
